comparator.name: Earth Sciences, Economics and Sustainability (Aarde, Economie en Duurzaamheid)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER governing the current programme, checked 2026-09-25; current VU overview and programme chart consulted
comparator.route: Ordinary 180-EC full-time bachelor under the adopted 2026–27 OER; first-listed 6-EC third-year restricted elective Stedelijke uitdagingen
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER names ten compulsory 6-EC units in each of years one and two (60+60 EC). First year includes economics, global change, Earth, mathematics, sustainable land use, energy, modelling, soils and two distinct climate-adaptation fieldwork preparation/execution units. Year two is 60 EC required: energy/resources, statistics, nature management, socioeconomic analysis, environmental economics, hydrology, GIS/Earth observation, land use/planning, hazards and spatial-solutions fieldwork. Year three is 24 EC compulsory (6 Big Data in Sustainability Science, 6 environmental ethics, 12 independent bachelor thesis), plus 6 EC chosen from two restricted modules (first-listed Stedelijke uitdagingen selected neutrally rather than adding a thesis extension), plus 30 EC genuinely free first-semester minor space. The OER thus supplies a 150-EC major and 30 EC free space. Zero-credit language test, geoflex lectures and mentoring do not add to the 180 EC. The public study overview lists an earlier second-year subject mix and explicitly warns that old study-guide years two/three were not current; the adopted 2026–27 OER and its linked programme chart control the course reconstruction. The first- and second-year fieldwork are distinct credited compulsory units; the 12-EC thesis is not a third course added to a chosen 6-EC thesis extension.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three defensible UCR programmes have distinct evidenced organising questions and pairwise differences of at least four courses: integrated Earth–economics sustainability, flood/water adaptation with spatial data, and resource/energy decisions with economics. Additional programme-interest rows describe examples and outcomes rather than requiring extra UCR directions.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address global climatic change; UCR emphasizes anthropogenic climate impacts.
Both introduce interacting Earth systems and field observation.
Both use models of Earth and climate systems.
Both investigate soils, hydrology and the landscape through field/lab methods.
Both study water management; UCR is focused on deltas and flood adaptation.
Both train in GIS and Earth-observation datasets.
Both analyse natural hazards and risk reduction.
VU has a specified first-year climate-adaptation field course; related UCR field activities are not the same credited placement.
VU requires its own specified 6-EC spatial-solutions fieldwork; UCR delta research and field activities are related, not an exact equivalent.
Both engage environmental constraints on land use, though UCR emphasizes ecology rather than land-use planning.
Both examine lower-carbon energy transition; UCR designs renewable systems.
Both examine energy and Earth resources; UCR focuses on geoscience research.
Both address sustainability and nature governance; UCR course develops competing governance approaches, not a direct nature-management practicum.
Both address planning and collective decisions about sustainability; UCR emphasizes policy governance, not technical spatial planning.
Both examine environmental values and responsibilities, but UCR frames them through social movements and environmental justice rather than professional ethics.
Both teach economic foundations of choices under scarcity.
Both provide mathematics for environmental/economic quantitative work.
Both examine socio-economic choices under scarcity, though UCR focuses on microeconomics and behaviour.
Both can analyse environmental externalities and public economics; UCR does not offer a dedicated environmental-economics course.
Chosen 6-EC urban challenges module remains programme-specific; related sustainability governance and economics courses are not the same urban module.
Both plan/applied research for a sustainability question, but UCR project is not VU fieldwork preparation.
Both use statistical analysis, with UCR teaching general probability and statistics.
Both develop data analysis, though UCR machine learning uses general applications and not a dedicated sustainability-science big-data course.
The compulsory independent 12-EC VU bachelor thesis cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or UCR’s optional research element.
Genuine open 30-EC minor space remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.

notes.text: The adopted VU programme integrates 150 EC of specified Earth, economics, spatial data, policy, credited fieldwork and a 12-EC independent thesis with a 30-EC free minor. UCR offers substantial related coursework and project/field experiences, but its six-semester alternatives do not replicate VU’s named fieldwork units, dedicated environmental-economics sequence or required individual AED thesis; pairwise rows indicate overlap without claiming transfer equivalence.
